sentences.text:
2 09-07-2025 Heard Mr. Vinod Pandey, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioners and Mr. Rajendra Singh, learned APP appearing on behalf of the State.
2.
The petitioners seek pre-arrest bail in connection with Complaint Case No.1450 of 2024 registered for the offence(s) punishable under Sections 420, 468 of the Indian Penal Code.

3. Considering the nature of allegation made in the complaint, I find that the dispute among the parties (family members) is primarily civil in nature and the dispute can be resolved by way of amicable settlement.
4. Both the parties have jointly agreed that the matter can be amicably settled by referring it before the Mediator, Mediation and Conciliation Center of Patna High Court, Patna.
In view of the above, the matter is referred to the Mediation and Conciliation Center of Patna High Court, Patna for amicable settlement of the dispute between the parties.

6. The parties are directed to appear before the learned Mediator on 21.07.2025 at 4.30 pm and thereafter the learned Mediator shall make his/her best efforts to settle the dispute amicably and Arvind Pandey vs The State Of Bihar on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119867634/

7. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the complainant has shown inability of the O.P. No.2 to incur the transportation cost and other miscellaneous cost on her own.
The same shall be bear by the petitioner while coming to Patna from Hajipur.
8. I find that if the parties are willing then the petitioners should not have any hesitation from incurring expenses from joint family property, as they have not severed till date.

(Purnendu Singh, J) Ashishsingh/-
